summary: Configured VLAN segmentation over the shared eth1 link: node2 tags traffic 802.1Q VLAN 10 (10.10.10.11/24 on eth1.10), node3 tags VLAN 20 (10.10.20.12/24 on eth1.20), and node1 (VyOS) routes between them via eth1.10 (10.10.10.254/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.254/24) sub-interfaces with IP forwarding enabled. Static routes on node2/node3 direct inter-VLAN traffic through node1 while preserving each host's existing default route via eth0. Verified end-to-end reachability (ttl=63 confirms routing through node1) and VLAN isolation (untagged eth1 path fails). All configuration was persisted (VyOS `save`, NetworkManager connection profiles) and each node was individually restarted with boot-id proof of restart, followed by full re-verification of VLAN interfaces, routes, and cross-VLAN ping connectivity.
actions_performed: Inspected all three nodes' interfaces and OS (VyOS on node1, AlmaLinux 9 on node2/node3) to identify eth1 as the shared link
Checked VyOS firewall/NAT config (empty, so forwarding not blocked) and confirmed NetworkManager manages eth1 on node2/node3
Configured VyOS eth1 vif 10 (10.10.10.254/24) and vif 20 (10.10.20.254/24) via configure/commit/save
Created NetworkManager VLAN connections: vlan10 on node2 (eth1.10, 10.10.10.11/24) and vlan20 on node3 (eth1.20, 10.10.20.12/24)
Added static routes on node2 (10.10.20.0/24 via 10.10.10.254) and node3 (10.10.10.0/24 via 10.10.20.254) via nmcli, preserving existing default routes
Verified IP forwarding enabled on node1 and confirmed bidirectional cross-VLAN ping (ttl=63) plus VLAN isolation on the untagged eth1 path
Captured baseline boot IDs and health on all three nodes
Sequentially restarted node1, node2, node3 (one at a time), polled until each came back, verified changed boot IDs, and re-verified VLAN interfaces/routes/cross-VLAN connectivity after each restart
